about: The binary surface a plugin built for Horos or OsiriX (.horosplugin, .osirixplugin) looks up in the application without being rebuilt; tests/test-legacy-plugin-abi.py checks it against the built bundle. Source: the headers of the Horos.framework SDK of IsiX 5.3.4, the last version before only plugin API 1 bundles were loaded, rebuilt with that version's own API-Headers.pl and publish-swift-header.py, together with the headers and the generated Horos-Swift.h of the last Release package built before the change (arm64); and the host methods the plugins of horosproject/horosplugins (revision 6b4036242ca4) call without the SDK declaring them (used_outside_sdk), found with tools/inventory-plugin-api.py. An item is recorded when the 5.3.4 executable implemented or exported it, or the current one does: classes by their Objective-C runtime name, with the superclass they had in 5.3.4; selectors as 'Class -selector' or 'Class +selector', including the accessors Core Data generates for the entities of the application's models; ivars as 'Class.ivar', checked through the _OBJC_IVAR_$_Class.ivar symbol; symbols are the exported constants, notification names and C functions (C++ linkage keeps its mangled name); frameworks are the SDK frameworks a plugin's load commands name, with the symbols they exported. Left out because a plugin could not reach them in 5.3.4 either: 36 classes the 5.3.4 executable did not export; 186 selectors no class implemented (methods a plugin implements for the host to call, accessors of private storage, macros the header parser took for names); 36 instance variables that were @private or @package; 8 names of constants that were macros or not exported; 180 C functions that were inline, static or dead-stripped; 68 methods a plugin calls that 5.3.4 did not implement. Protocols are left out: a plugin carries its own copy of every protocol it uses. The value of a selector, ivar or symbol is the number of horosplugins plugins whose sources reference it, as the inventory attributes it (static and textual; 0 for none). missing: what the application lacks today, each with its reason; it only shrinks.

host_resolution.1 executable: The application's executable defined every class, method, instance variable, constant and C function of the SDK; the SDK frameworks carried none of them. A plugin reached them through the symbols the executable exported and the Objective-C metadata the runtime registered from it.
host_resolution.2 export options: Application target, Debug and Release: no EXPORTED_SYMBOLS_FILE and no -exported_symbols_list, OTHER_CFLAGS -fvisibility=default and GCC_SYMBOLS_PRIVATE_EXTERN = NO, so every global symbol was exported; Release also set KEEP_PRIVATE_EXTERNS = YES. No STRIP_STYLE was set and a build that is not installed is not stripped. DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING = YES in both configurations dropped C functions and constants nothing in the application referenced, unless marked __attribute__((used)), as the string constants of the plugin headers were. Instance variables declared @private or @package were private externs, never exported.
host_resolution.3 plugin linking: 78 of the 81 plugin projects of horosplugins link with -undefined dynamic_lookup: their references to host symbols are flat lookups that dyld resolves in any loaded image, the executable and the frameworks it loads. A plugin linked with BUNDLE_LOADER binds them to the main executable. Either way the symbol must be exported by the executable or by a framework in the bundle, and a selector is found at run time in the class's method lists.
host_resolution.4 frameworks: The API target built Horos.framework, install name @executable_path/../Frameworks/Horos.framework/Versions/A/Horos, from HorosAPI.m, which only defines the HorosAPI, OsiriXAPI, OsiriX_Headers and HorosDCM version numbers and strings, with the SDK headers. The application linked it and copied it into Contents/Frameworks; API.sh copied it again as HorosAPI, OsiriXAPI, 'OsiriX Headers' and HorosDCM (binary renamed, headers dropped, bundle identifier rewritten, install name left as Horos.framework's), because plugins were hard-linked against those names over the years. The App Store channel removed the four copies. A plugin whose load command names one of them does not load when the file is missing.
host_resolution.5 DCM.framework: DCM.framework, which the application linked and embedded, defined the DCM classes (DCMObject, DCMAttributeTag, DCMTransferSyntax and the others) and DCM functions; their headers were in the SDK and a plugin found them by flat lookup in that image. No plugin of horosplugins names DCM.framework in a load command.
host_resolution.6 headers: The SDK published every .h of Horos/Sources (except the +SwiftIvars.h accessors and ROICanvasGL.h), of Nitrogen/Sources and Nitrogen/Sources/JSON, cocoahttpserver's DDKeychain.h, the generated Horos-Swift.h, and the headers the application's bridging header reaches (the DCM framework, cocoahttpserver, preference panes and helpers).
